newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says long-term 3 pct growth needed for jobs.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says long-term 3 pct growth needed for jobs.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Wednesday his country needed growth of at least three percent over a sustained period to help tackle unemployment.

"If we want to confirm the reversal of the employment trend which we are already starting to see, meaning we destroy fewer jobs and start to create more of them, we need growth," Juppe said in an interview on FR3 French television.
"We need regular growth over a long period and growth of at least three percent, and I believe this is possible because we are nearly there," he added.

Juppe was speaking four days ahead of an early parliamentary election at which France's 12.8 percent record jobless rate looms large in many voters' minds at a time when France is tightening its belt to help qualify for European monetary union.

The government has said growth, forecast at a minimum 2.3 percent this year and 2.8 percent next year, will allow it to cut public deficits and qualify for the single currenncy without any additional austerity measures.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told a meeting in Washington last month that growth should reach 2.5 percent around the first half of this year before rising to three percent at year-end.
Opposition Socialists led by Lionel Jospin have called for a new solidarity and growth pact between nations joining the euro to make that project an engine for growth needed to boost jobs.
